In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CTCF/cohesion mediated chromatin organization is critical to the HOXA gene expression and cell-type specific spatial collinearity in human fibroblastic cells.
CTCF and Cohesin coordinate the HOXA cluster higher- order chromatic structure, which may be a key mechanism for the cell-type specific HOXA gene expression.
CTCF and its associated cohesin complex play a critical role in maintaining cell-type specific higher- order chromosomal architecture of the HOXA cluster and the associated gene expression patterns.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CTCF and its cohesin partner are critical for the establishment and maintenance of cell-type specific HOXA gene expression and chromatin architecture in human fibroblastic cells.
CTCF and Cohesin coordinate the chromatin structure of HOXA cluster, and the chromatin structure is important for cell type specific expression of HOXA cluster.
CTCF is a critical regulator for the higher-order chromosomal structure of the HOX gene cluster, and this chromatin organization is important for the expression of HOX genes during development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell-type specific chromosomal architecture is a key factor in regulating the spatial collineary of HOX gene clusters.
the CTCF/cohesion mediated chromatin structure of HOXA cluster is cell-type specific and plays a critical role in maintaining cell-type specific expression of HOX genes.
